questions.stem: Choose the correct tense: 'By the time I ______ home, she had already left.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'BY THE TIME + simple past (reached), + past perfect (had left).' Rule: when 'by the time' refers to a past situation, the main clause uses past perfect (had + V3) and the 'by the time' clause uses simple past.

questions.stem: Choose the correct tense: 'I ______ this book for the past three hours.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS = have/has been + V-ing. Used for actions that started in the past and CONTINUE TO THE PRESENT, especially with durations like 'for three hours,' 'since morning.' 'I HAVE BEEN READING this book for the past three hours' (and still am).

questions.stem: Choose the correct verb: 'Look! The cat ______ up the tree.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Look!' is a signal that something is happening RIGHT NOW → Present Continuous. 'Look! The cat IS CLIMBING up the tree.' Other 'happening now' signals: listen!, watch!, here comes...!, can you see...?

questions.stem: Choose the correct tense: 'She ______ this company since 2010.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. SINCE + year/point of time → use PRESENT PERFECT (has/have + V3) for ongoing situations. 'She HAS WORKED for this company since 2010' = started in 2010 and still works there. Compare: 'She WORKED for the company for 10 years' (and no longer does) = simple past.

questions.stem: Choose the correct tense: 'If I ______ a millionaire, I would travel the world.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. TYPE 2 CONDITIONAL (hypothetical present/future): If + past simple/were, would + base verb. For 'to be,' use 'WERE' (not 'was') for all persons in formal English: 'If I WERE a millionaire.' This is the subjunctive mood. 'If I was' is acceptable in informal speech.

questions.stem: Choose the correct tense: 'I ______ you if I had known you were in trouble.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. TYPE 3 CONDITIONAL (impossible past, regret): If + past perfect (had known), would have + V3 (would have helped). 'I WOULD HAVE HELPED you if I had known...' = I didn't help because I didn't know. Past condition, past hypothetical result.

questions.stem: Choose the correct tense: 'We ______ this project by next Monday.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. FUTURE PERFECT = will have + V3. Used for actions that will be completed BEFORE a specific future time/event. 'We WILL HAVE FINISHED this project BY next Monday' = by the deadline, the project will already be done.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS correctly?

options.option_text: She had been waiting for two hours when the train finally arrived.
She has been waiting for two hours.
She was waiting for two hours when the train arrived.
She had waited for two hours when the train arrived.

questions.explanation: A is correct. PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS = had been + V-ing. Shows: an action that was ongoing for a period BEFORE another past event occurred. 'She HAD BEEN WAITING for two hours WHEN the train arrived.' The waiting lasted until the train's arrival.

questions.stem: Identify the tense used: 'He will be sleeping at midnight.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. FUTURE CONTINUOUS = will be + V-ing. 'He WILL BE SLEEPING at midnight' = at midnight (future time), he will be in the middle of sleeping (ongoing). Compare: Future Simple 'He will sleep at midnight' (he will start sleeping at midnight); Future Continuous (he will already be asleep at midnight).

questions.stem: Choose the correct tense for a historical fact: 'The Indian Constitution ______ on 26 January 1950.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. SIMPLE PAST is used for historical events with specific dates: 'The Indian Constitution CAME INTO EFFECT on 26 January 1950.' When a specific past date is mentioned ('on 26 January 1950'), always use simple past — never present perfect ('has come into effect').
